pairs.reason: Active employee schedule slot guard exists in both generated and Wrangler migration tracks.
Coupon usage refund release marker exists in both tracks; SQL differs only where each track has different timestamp columns available.
Money cents retirement rollout guard exists in both tracks; it blocks destructive table rebuild rollout until audit coverage is present and clean.
Percentage discount values are preserved in explicit basis-point columns before polymorphic discount_value REAL columns are retired.
Money cents cutover removes legacy REAL money columns after clean rollout and percentage-bps audit gates, retaining cents and basis-point columns only.
Market checkout child orders now retain total_amount_cents only; API responses derive decimal totals from cents.
Payment idempotency keys are unique when present and backup timestamp fields move to integer millisecond columns in both migration tracks.
images.uploaded_by moves from INTEGER to TEXT so it can store users.id UUID v7 values for the image-processor upload path (issue #56).
menu_items.image_id records the owning images.id value so menu image replacement can delete the previous image.
Duplicate seat numbers are reconciled before both migration tracks enforce one seat number per table.
menu_items.name_en and categories.name_en back the admin menu forms' English-name inputs, which previously had no columns and were silently discarded (#107).

categories.item_count is dropped in both tracks: only createMenuItem ever wrote it, so deletes, availability toggles and category moves left it stale, and item counts are now derived live from menu_items (#84).

Menu item soft deletion now writes menu_items.deleted_at_ms instead of the sort_order=-1 convention; rows deleted under the old marker are backfilled so they stay deleted once reads filter on deleted_at_ms (#80).
Both tracks add the same pending QR staging columns and partial unique indexes for two-phase rotation.

freshOnly.reason: Fresh baseline owns the service_bookings overlap guard; the legacy migration track does not currently carry the service_bookings table migration.

Fresh API D1 owns group_orders for guest-hosted group orders; the local management/legacy D1 does not carry group_orders, and the packages/database legacy track has incompatible historical group_orders definitions rather than a verified live schema.

Fresh API D1 owns the shared customization option groups (option_groups / option_choices / menu_item_option_groups / menu_item_option_choice_overrides). The legacy management D1 carries neither menu_items nor restaurants in the shape these reference, so there is no paired legacy migration.
Phase A backfills one independent option group set per menu item, so group public_id values such as spice must be reusable within a restaurant while choice public_id remains unique within its group.

legacyOnly.reason: Legacy operational performance-index migration predates this guard and is reviewed as legacy-only.
